name: Biffy Clyro
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Three teenagers from Ayrshire spent three Beggars Banquet albums hiding their choruses on purpose. Then Simon Neil decided they were the best band in the world, and they went on to headline Reading.

hero.by: Biffy Clyro at Reading Festival, August 2021. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Screwfish, from Ayr to Glasgow
eras.text: Simon Neil was 15 when he started a band with drummer Ben Johnston, and Ben's twin James soon took the bass. They studied in Glasgow, played its small rooms, and got signed after a Beggars Banquet scout caught them on the unsigned stage at T in the Park.

years.src: Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro · Wikipedia: Simon Neil
years.h: First gig as Screwfish, at a youth centre in East Kilbride
years.p: Simon Neil and Ben Johnston open for a band called Pink Kross at the Key Youth Centre. James Johnston joins on bass, and the trio spends two years rehearsing, writing and playing covers.

years.h: The trio moves to Glasgow and becomes Biffy Clyro
years.p: Neil studies at the University of Glasgow; the twins go to Stow College. Nobody has ever given a straight answer on the name.
years.xp: The band have told it as a footballer for Ayr United, a spoonerism of a "Cliffy Biro" Cliff Richard pen, an acronym, a 17th-century Finnish footballer, and a Scotsman who built his own rocket. Ben Johnston once said it joins a spy's nickname with Clyro, the Welsh village where their families went on holiday. Neil just calls it "a stupid name."

years.h: Iname, the first single, comes out on Aereogramme's label
years.p: New manager Dee Bahl gets the band onto Babi Yaga, run by Glasgow band Aereogramme. Jim Gellatly at Northsound Radio gives Biffy its first radio play.

years.h: A Stow College student label puts out thekidswhopoptodaywillrocktomorrow
years.p: Electric Honey, the label run out of the twins' college, picks Biffy for its next release. BBC Radio Scotland's Vic Galloway plays it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro · Beggars Banquet: Blackened Sky
years.h: A Beggars Banquet scout sees them on T in the Park's unsigned stage
years.p: A few days before the EP comes out, the band plays the Unsigned Bands stage at Scotland's biggest festival. Beggars Banquet signs them soon after.

eras.title: Choruses four and a half minutes in
eras.text: Three albums for Beggars Banquet, each stranger than the last, built a loyal crowd that knew every time change. Neil wanted Biffy to be a cult band like Fugazi or Shudder to Think, and for a while that's what it was.

years.h: Justboy gets re-recorded as a Beggars single
years.p: Songs from the student-label EP get second lives on Beggars: 27 in April, Justboy in October, 57 the following February.

yt: Live at the Arches, Glasgow, November 14, 2001
years.h: The Arches, Glasgow, on a year of constant touring
years.p: After a Kerrang! package tour with Sunna and Hell Is for Heroes, the band starts its first UK headline run. A fan's tape from the Arches survives.

years.src: Wikipedia: Blackened Sky · Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro · Vice: Rank Your Records
years.h: Blackened Sky, written when Neil was 16 and 17
years.p: Produced with Chris Sheldon, the debut reaches No. 78. Reviews were mixed; AllMusic gave it one and a half stars.
years.xp: Neil told Noisey the songs carried "that real naivety" of a teenager. Nine days after release the band supported [[Weezer|6fe07aa5-fec0-4eca-a456-f29bff451b04]] at the Barrowland in Glasgow.

years.h: Milo Manara draws the cover for The Vertigo of Bliss
years.p: Recorded at Linford Manor in Milton Keynes with strings added, the second album reaches No. 48. The erotic cover by the Italian comics artist drew complaints.
years.xp:
Neil was annoyed by the reaction. People called it schoolboy stuff, he told ShortList, when judging it on a shallow level was the schoolboy move.

The Guardian gave the album four stars, calling it "inventive and sublime". Oceansize's Mike Vennart, later Biffy's touring guitarist, called it "pretty much the perfect album."

years.src: Wikipedia: Infinity Land · Vice: Rank Your Records
years.h: Infinity Land takes its title from a Jeffrey Dahmer book
years.p: Recorded at Monnow Valley in Wales: songs in 5/4, constant key changes, and a hidden poem read by Neil after about 18 minutes of silence. The last of the three Beggars albums.
years.xp:
Neil explained the title as Dahmer's word for his idea of heaven, which was grim. "It could sound hopeful," he said, "but when you know what it's referring to, it becomes quite sinister."

Ben Johnston told Noisey this was where the band found its sound, and Neil started singing in his own Scottish accent.

years.h: A [[Franz Ferdinand|aa7a2827-f74b-473c-bd79-03d065835cf7]] cover live from Maida Vale for Zane Lowe
years.p: The band plays Take Me Out on BBC Radio 1. Lowe would premiere almost every Biffy lead single from here on.

years.src: Wikipedia: Marmaduke Duke · Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro
years.h: Neil's side project Marmaduke Duke tours with the twins as its rhythm section
years.p: The Magnificent Duke, made with JP Reid of Sucioperro, comes out in 4,000 copies. Ben and James play drums and bass on the road.

years.cap: Queen Margaret Union, Glasgow, Freshers' Week
years.h: Infinity Land in full at King Tut's Wah Wah Hut
years.p: The band plays the whole album at the Glasgow club. It wouldn't do it again until 2024.

eras.title: Wanting to share
eras.text: Neil's mother died between the third and fourth albums, and he came out of it with a different ambition. The band left Beggars for a Warner offshoot, cut the choruses earlier, and within three years had a Top 10 single and a Mercury nomination.

years.big: "I think we're the best band in the fucking world."
q: We started out with an aim to annoy.
years.src: Louder: Simon Neil on the band's early days · Wikipedia: Puzzle
years.h: After his mother's death, Neil decides to compete
years.p: Simon Neil, recalling to Louder the point when his mother Eleanor died. The band leaves Beggars Banquet for 14th Floor, part of Warner Bros.
years.xp:
Before that, Neil said, he only wanted "a bunch of people in each town who cared about our band." Watching weaker bands do well while he reassessed his life changed that.

The first song he wrote afterwards was Living Is a Problem Because Everything Dies, which opens Puzzle. "We started out with an aim to annoy," he said, "and when that disappeared, we flourished!"

years.src: Wikipedia: Puzzle · Vice: Rank Your Records
years.h: Puzzle goes to No. 2, with a Storm Thorgerson sleeve
years.p: Made in British Columbia with Garth Richardson, mixed by Andy Wallace, mostly about the death of Neil's mother. Kerrang! and Rock Sound both named it album of the year.
years.xp:
The band had 40 tracks to pick from and recorded with composer Graeme Revell and the Seattle Symphony Orchestra. The sleeve still carries the Beggars Banquet logo.

It's certified Platinum in the UK.
play: Living Is a Problem Because Everything Dies

years.h: Opening for Muse at the new Wembley, and for the Rolling Stones
years.p: Big support slots with [[Muse|9c9f1380-2516-4fc9-a3e6-f9f61941d090]], [[The Who|9fdaa16b-a6c4-4831-b87c-bc9ca8ce7eaa]], [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|8bfac288-ccc5-448d-9573-c33ea2aa5c30]] and [[The Rolling Stones|b071f9fa-14b0-4217-8e97-eb41da73f598]], plus Download, Glastonbury, Reading and Leeds, and a seventh T in the Park.

years.h: Mountains is Biffy's first Top 10 single
years.p: A stand-alone single, it reaches No. 5. In December the band headlines Glasgow's 10,000-capacity SECC, its biggest show yet.

years.src: Wikipedia: Only Revolutions · Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro
years.h: Only Revolutions borrows a Mark Z. Danielewski title
years.p: [[Josh Homme|dbecd515-aac9-4e7b-808e-bca22809c316]] plays a guitar solo on Bubbles, and David Campbell arranges strings on six songs. It's nominated for the 2010 Mercury Prize.
years.xp:
James Johnston called it a love record about Neil's new marriage, written to see an argument from both sides. Danielewski turned out to be a fan and came to a show.

Zane Lowe played That Golden Rule twice in a row on its first spin. The album reached No. 3 and went double platinum.

years.h: Fans fight the X Factor winner over Many of Horror
years.p: Matt Cardle releases the song as When We Collide and gets Christmas No. 1. A Facebook campaign pushes Biffy's original to No. 8, its highest chart spot.

eras.title: A double album and a sober drummer
eras.text: With arenas filling, the band nearly broke during the Opposites sessions. It came out the other side with a first No. 1 album, a Reading and Leeds headline and, by 2017, the top of the bill at Download.

years.h: 130,000 people over two nights with the Foo Fighters
years.p: Biffy supports [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] at the Milton Keynes Bowl, then headlines Sonisphere at Knebworth a week later.

years.big: "It was me that was going to f**k it all up."
years.h: Ben Johnston's drinking nearly ends the band in Santa Monica
years.p: Ben Johnston to the Scotsman. Blackouts and missed flights came to a head during the Opposites sessions; he started going to AA in Los Angeles and has been sober since.
years.xp:
He fell during a blackout in Santa Monica and cut his ear, and woke to Neil hammering on his door. He told the paper he'd half-expected to go home "with no record here. And no band."

James got a Robert Burns poem the twins recited at school tattooed down his side for his brother. Neil told the Scotsman his wife suffered three miscarriages in the same stretch.

years.src: Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro · Vice: Rank Your Records · Wikipedia: Simon Neil
years.h: Opposites is Biffy's first No. 1 album
years.p: A double album with tap dancers, a mariachi band and bagpipes in it. The next day Zane Lowe announces the band as Reading and Leeds headliners; they play on August 25.
years.xp: "If you're in a rock band and you can't make a double album then fuck off," Neil told Noisey. Biffy also won Best British Band at the NME Awards that year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Biffy Clyro · Vice: Rank Your Records
years.h: After a year off, Ellipsis goes to No. 1
years.p: Produced by Rich Costey. Neil called it the most modern version of the band.

years.h: Saturday headliners at Download, sixth time on the bill
years.p: Their first main-stage headline at the festival, the same month as a Glastonbury slot.

eras.title: Back under the old name
eras.text: The band made a film, a pandemic album played to an empty Barrowland, and kept a run of No. 1s going. In 2024 it went back to the three Beggars records, and in 2025 played a secret show as Screwfish.

yt: Many of Horror, MTV Unplugged at the Roundhouse
years.h: MTV Unplugged: Live at the Roundhouse
years.p: The acoustic London show comes out on album and DVD, followed by a European tour of the same set.

years.h: Balance, Not Symmetry: a film built around a Biffy soundtrack
years.p: Directed by Jamie Adams and starring Laura Harrier, it premieres at the Edinburgh Film Festival; the 17-song soundtrack came out in May.

years.h: A Celebration of Endings waits out lockdown, then hits No. 1
years.p: Pushed back from May by the pandemic, it's the third straight No. 1. With the arena tour cancelled, the band plays it in full on a livestream from Glasgow's Barrowland.

years.h: The Myth of the Happily Ever After
years.p: A companion record to A Celebration of Endings. Amazon's documentary Cultural Sons of Scotland follows its making in February 2022.

years.src: Louder: Simon Neil on the band's early days · Beggars Banquet: Blackened Sky · Wikipedia: Infinity Land
years.h: A Celebration of Beginnings: the Beggars albums, three nights each city
years.p: The band plays Blackened Sky, The Vertigo of Bliss and Infinity Land in full in Glasgow and London. Beggars reissues them on October 18.

years.h: Screwfish plays a secret show at SWG3, Glasgow
years.p: Under their first name, the band debuts A Little Love and 1001. A month later they play Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage.

years.h: Futique makes it four UK No. 1s in a row
years.p: The tenth album also tops the Scottish chart.

years.h: James Johnston steps off the road for treatment
years.p: The band said he would miss upcoming tours to seek treatment for addiction linked to long-standing mental health problems. Naomi Macleod, of Neil's side band Empire State Bastard, covers bass.
